scope: R150 event-level FA/USP decomposition (baseline mode plus the R126 attention profiler)

corrections.wrapper_overhead: the FA wrapper adds only about 130 ms per step, not the ~745 ms that the R149 Python-level number implied; the R150 number is the precise one because the profiler wraps the 910A entry point directly
corrections.fa_kernel: the 910A FA kernel itself is 7606.7 ms per step, which is 42.2 percent of the step

ten_second_arithmetic.verdict: a zero-cost attention kernel would still leave 10.42 s, so 10 s requires eliminating essentially all of the attention kernel cost (7.607 s today) and then finding another 0.42 s; no 2x-style kernel improvement can reach it

numerically_free_headroom.note: these are the only candidates that do not change arithmetic; together they are about 1.5 s, far short of the 8.03 s needed

conclusion: 10 s/step remains unreachable under the current contract. R150 refines the R149 numbers and removes the hope that wrapper overhead was a hidden win. The realistic floor stays about 12 s with a 2x FA kernel plus linears at their measured standalone rates.
awaiting: user decision among: revised ~12 s target / authorise a mathematical-contract change / authorise a different hardware or parallelism plan
